newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - CFDs tumble 13 cts, mogas down $4.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - CFDs tumble 13 cts, mogas down $4.

text.p: European oil swaps corrected lower on Friday after a week of mostly firmer prices.
Weaker Brent, Iraqi oil exports and faltering gasoline demand also undermined prices but activity was thin with much of Europe on holiday.
Brent CFDs tumbled 13 cents a barrel to 27 cents under October for next week's dates with the following three weeks a similar amount lower at 28 cents, 30 cents and 30 cents under respectively.

The flat weekly CFD structure was in contrast to most other areas of the market. Monthly CFDs against the IPE remain in contango with discounts around 28 cents (September), 27 cents (October), 22 cents (Q4 97), 10 cents (Q1 98) and nine cents (1998).
Gasoline slipped $4 a tonne to trade at $200 for September and talk close to $190 for October but the only trade reported on physical barges was at $226.50.
Naphtha fell $2 a tonne to $187.50 for September amid poor demand and falling Brent.
Gas oil swaps were little changed despite the weaker tone on IPE gas oil futures. Jet premiums were unchanged following several days of weaker prices on the fourth quarter.
Heavy fuel slipped $1 a tonne to $94.25 for September barges with low sulphur some $4.50 higher.
The fourth quarter barges were valued around $97.75 by the close, having traded earlier at $97.50.
